_comment: capability-catalog declarations — the DATA half of plugin/scripts/capability-catalog.sh.
Why this file exists: the 10 declaration tables below used to be bash `declare -A` arrays
inside capability-catalog.sh. They are DATA (file -> question / cadence / invalidation /
last-reaffirmed / matching / consumer / shipping / public-entrypoint), not code, so they live
here and are read by the TypeScript renderer plugin/scripts/capability-catalog.ts.
The old form was a command-substitution hazard: a bash double-quoted value is evaluated at
load time (round 143 — a backtick value ran a whole doc-check suite on every catalog load and
its multiline output broke the tab-separated rows). JSON values are never evaluated, so that
hazard class is structurally gone; the renderer nonetheless still enforces the invariant
fail-closed (CAUSE=data-value-command-substitution) so a migrated-away hazard does not become
a permanently-green check with nothing to observe.
Keys: the 10 table names, plus underscore-prefixed keys (like this one) which the renderer
ignores. Entry values are character-for-character what bash evaluated the old arrays to —
including the LAST-WINS resolution of 16 duplicate assignments that existed in the shell
source (12 in QUESTION, 1 each in CADENCE, INVALIDATION, LAST_REAFFIRMED, MATCHING). That
collapse is verified against a bash evaluation of the original declare blocks, not assumed.
Editing: a NEW plugin/scripts script must add its QUESTION plus CADENCE, INVALIDATION,
LAST_REAFFIRMED and MATCHING entries here (and CONSUMER if it has one). THIS FILE, not the
.sh, is the registration point — select-static-checks-for-touches.ts names it in
NEW_SCRIPT_REGISTRATION_REQUIRED so a new-script task must declare it in Touches.

QUESTION.release-cut.sh: How does a RELEASE CUT — the whole SPEC §4/§12 sequence, not just its last three steps — happen as ONE re-runnable command instead of a remembered list? Measured 2026-09-24 (the v0.12.0 cut): ~12 hand-steps, of which two bit — release-branch-finish.sh --cut requires HEAD == base, so it could not be run from the main checkout (HEAD=author) and the cut moved into an INDEPENDENT CLONE, where the finish record landed in that clone's .quay/ (invisible to the main ledger AC-320 reads); and the next-version bump necessarily staled the closure-ratchet baseline, which the prose never mentioned. This command does the sequence in one invocation: preflight (tag free / version-consistent / clean tree / develop not behind the remote) -> a LINKED WORKTREE off develop (never a clone, never a branch switch in the main checkout) -> release-branch-finish.sh --cut --tag (merge back + tag the merge point + delete) -> push -> dispatch release.yml and echo the run URL -> next-version bump on develop + stamp-version + closure-ratchet re-anchor -> remove the worktree, each stage with its own CAUSE= and exit code, plus an --dry-run that prints every step (including the ledger's ABSOLUTE landing path) while writing nothing?
